prompt: Predict what `ksnprintf` does for `ksnprintf(buf, 8, "%05d|%x", -42, 255)` and related calls. The contract follows C's `snprintf`.

trace.label: [text] produced by `%05d` with -42 (width counts the sign)
[return value] of the call above (full output is `-0042|ff`)
[strlen(buf)] afterwards (size 8 leaves room for the NUL)

explain: Zero padding goes after the sign, so -42 with width 5 is `-0042`. `%5d` pads with spaces on the left. The full output `-0042|ff` is 8 characters, and snprintf always returns the length the output would have had, so the return value is 8 even though the buffer holds only size - 1 = 7 characters plus the NUL (`-0042|f`). Callers compare the return value with `size` to detect truncation, so it must keep counting after the buffer is full.
